fields.narrative_intro: *A bewildered person and an exasperated person discuss A/I shutting down inside a spam folder that has achieved sentience and is very upset about it.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
BEWILDERED PERSON: "A/I is shutting down after 25 years."
EXASPERATED PERSON: "The privacy collective providing secure, non-commercial tools?"
fields.panel2:
[build]
BEWILDERED PERSON: "They’re preparing backups for blogs, mailboxes, and websites."
EXASPERATED PERSON: "At least users get warning before the door closes."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
BEWILDERED PERSON: "It followed threats—and a 'global terrorist organization' designation."
EXASPERATED PERSON: "For secure, non-commercial digital tools?"
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The characters stare silently as autistici.org flashes “UNREACHABLE”; nearby phishing emails glow “DELIVERED.”]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
EXASPERATED PERSON: "The privacy tools need evacuation plans; spam gets automatic renewal?"
BEWILDERED PERSON: "Spam has better continuity planning."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The sentient folder proudly labels a 25-year archive “Continuity Plan”; every message says “FINAL WARNING: YOUR ACCOUNT CLOSES TOMORROW.”]

narrative_summary: A shutdown-prone privacy infrastructure is contrasted with a spam folder whose fake account warnings have enjoyed flawless 25-year continuity.
rationale: Candidate 4 turns the story’s shutdown, unreachable domain, and 25-year history into a clean, escalating contrast: privacy infrastructure needs evacuation plans while spam enjoys continuity. The final archive of perpetual “FINAL WARNING” messages is a specific visual button rather than a restatement.
place: inside a spam folder that has achieved sentience and is very upset about it
hat_pair: crash helmet made entirely of bubble wrap
foam graduation cap with a tiny diploma scroll taped to the top
